text_3: Swiss dramatic soprano Diana Lamar, of Bulgarian heritage, is acclaimed for her interpretations of Verdi, Puccini, Strauss, and Cherubini, and praised for her “full-bodied, polished voice with a velvety timbre.”
text_4: Highlights of her 2026/27 season include Elektra at Teatro Verdi Trieste, Aida in Graz and Gdansk, Katarina Ismailova in Stuttgart, Norma at the Palacio de Bellas Artes in Mexico City, and returns to Wrocław Opera as Tosca and Madama Butterfly as well as to Gdansk as Aida and Maddalena (Andrea Chénier).
text_5: Recent engagements include Elektra in Mexico City, Trieste, at the Festival Internacional Cervantino, and Daegu Opera House; Tosca in Wrocław, Modena, Lima, Trier, and Messina, as well as in The Seven Deaths of Maria Callas at Deutsche Oper Berlin. Other roles include Madama Butterfly, Senta (Der fliegende Holländer) at NCPA Beijing, Medea, and Lisa (The Queen of Spades).
text_6: In concert, her repertoire includes Strauss’ Vier letzte Lieder, Mahler’s Rückert-Lieder, and Verdi’s Requiem. She has collaborated with conductors and directors including Marcus Bosch, Christof Loy, Stefan Lano, Giancarlo Del Monaco, Marco Gandini, Plamen Kartalov, and Renata Scotto.
text_7: Diana Lamar holds Master’s degrees in Vocal Performance and Vocal Pedagogy from the Haute École de Musique de Genève. She is fluent in seven languages and is a recipient of the Maria Callas Tribute Prize (New York) and First Prize at the Concorso Internazionale per Cantanti Lirici “Città di Alcamo.”
